name: model-harvest
title: Unified Model Harvest — BioModels + PhysioNet into the HRA Model DB
question:
Can a single Step reproduce/refresh the unified HRA model DB
(datasets/model_hra_map.json) across every registered model source --
BioModels and, newly, PhysioNet -- incrementally and non-destructively, so
that running this study *is* the reproducibility hook for the whole DB,
not just a read of a static file?

study_card.goal: Expose viva_human_atlas.model_harvest.ModelHarvestStep as the model-harvest study's baseline: load (or, when asked, refresh) datasets/model_hra_map.json across the biomodels + physionet source registry and report total + per-source model counts plus the corpus coverage summary, so that running this study is how the unified DB gets reproduced or incrementally refreshed.
study_card.mechanism: ModelHarvestStep.update -> model_harvest.harvest: for each named source (biomodels, physionet) in the SOURCES registry, list_fn enumerates candidate items (BioModels search / PhysioNet DataCite DOI enumeration under the shared 10.13026 prefix), should_process(db, identifier, force) skips anything already keyed in the DB unless --force, and entry_fn upserts a per-source entry keyed by a stable identifier (BioModels IRI, PhysioNet content URL) -- so a plain rerun only harvests newly-posted models and a source refresh never touches another source's rows. PhysioNet entries are organ-mapped by physionet_organ_map.map_project_to_organs: a curated physiology-keyword -> UBERON table first (deterministic, offline), falling back to an LLM (claude-haiku-4-5) for the unmapped tail, both bound to HRA organs through the same hra_mapping.map_to_hra the BioModels path uses. With build_if_missing: false (this study's baseline), no network calls happen at all -- the Step just loads the committed DB via biomodel_hra.load_map and reports bh.summarize_map's coverage stats, so the study is network-free by default and only reaches out when explicitly told to refresh. scripts/harvest_models.py (the reproducible-refresh CLI) calls the exact same harvest() function, so the Step and the CLI cannot diverge.
study_card.expected_result: With build_if_missing: false, the baseline loads whatever is currently committed to datasets/model_hra_map.json and reports it verbatim: following the PhysioNet harvest run, the committed DB now spans both sources -- 1,576 models total, 1,096 repository=biomodels + 480 repository=physionet. Every existing BioModels row was preserved untouched; PhysioNet rows were incrementally upserted by identifier alongside them, confirming the source-registry mechanism this study's baseline reports on is exactly the one that produced the committed DB.
study_card.main_expert_question: Is loading the committed DB network-free (build_if_missing: false) the right default baseline for a study whose whole point is reproducibility -- or should the baseline itself force a live refresh each run, at the cost of losing the network-free guarantee that keeps offline CI green?

biological_summary:
BioModels and PhysioNet are curated from different angles -- BioModels
publishes quantitative systems-biology models (SBML/BioPAX, annotated for
biochemistry), PhysioNet publishes physiological signal/waveform datasets
and their companion models (ECG, EEG, respiratory, gait, and more) -- but
both describe things that live in a human organ, so both belong in the same
HRA-linked model DB. `model_harvest.harvest` treats them as interchangeable
entries in one source registry: each source contributes a `list_fn` (how to
enumerate its catalog -- BioModels search vs. PhysioNet's DataCite DOI
enumeration under the shared `10.13026` prefix) and an `entry_fn` (how to
build one DB row, including its HRA organ mapping), and `harvest()` upserts
every source's rows into the same `datasets/model_hra_map.json` keyed by a
stable per-source identifier. That keying is what makes the harvest
incremental and non-destructive: rerunning it only touches models new since
the last pass, and refreshing one source (say, adding PhysioNet for the
first time) can never overwrite or drop another source's rows. This study's
baseline is the `ModelHarvestStep` wired to both sources with
`build_if_missing: false`, so by default it just loads and reports whatever
is already committed -- the network-free, reproducible read every other
study and the Atlas Browser can depend on. Running it with a refresh flag
is the same Step actually doing the harvest: the mechanism this study
exercises is exactly the one that produced (and will keep extending)
`datasets/model_hra_map.json`.
readouts: n_models (total rows in datasets/model_hra_map.json across every registered source)
per_source.{biomodels,physionet} (row count contributed by each source, from a Counter over the repository field)
summary.{n_with_molecular,n_with_uberon,n_with_hrapop,coverage} (unchanged corpus-coverage stats from biomodel_hra.summarize_map, unaffected by which sources are loaded)
db_path (the committed dataset path the Step loaded, confirming the reproducibility hook points at the real file)

findings.statement:
The baseline (build_if_missing: false) loads the committed
datasets/model_hra_map.json network-free through the two-source
registry and reports it exactly as stored: 1,576 models -- 1,096
repository=biomodels + 480 repository=physionet, now that the
PhysioNet harvest has run against the committed DB. The BioModels-only
coverage stats are unchanged from biomodel-hra-map's
(n_with_molecular=978, n_with_hrapop=112), confirming PhysioNet rows
carry no molecular/HRApop annotations of their own; n_with_uberon rose
from 323 (BioModels alone) to 447 (323 BioModels + 124 PhysioNet,
offline keyword-mapped), showing the ModelHarvestStep's load path is a
pure superset wrapper over the existing BioModels DB plus the
newly-upserted PhysioNet rows, not a reinterpretation of either.

evidence.summary: n_models=1576, per_source={'biomodels': 1096, 'physionet': 480}. summary.n_with_molecular=978, n_with_uberon=447 (323 biomodels + 124 physionet), n_with_hrapop=112 -- molecular/HRApop stats identical to biomodel-hra-map's BioModels-only measurement (PhysioNet rows carry neither); n_with_uberon rose with the newly-added PhysioNet organ-tagged rows.

findings.statement:
The harvest is source-registry-driven and identifier-keyed, so it is
structurally incremental and non-destructive: should_process skips
anything already in the DB (a plain rerun only fetches newly-posted
models), and each source's entry_fn only ever upserts its own rows
under its own identifier scheme (BioModels IRIs vs. PhysioNet content
URLs), so a PhysioNet refresh cannot touch a BioModels row and vice
versa. That is what lets this one study stand in for "refresh the
whole unified DB" rather than needing a separate study per source.

evidence.summary: SOURCES registry has 2 entries (biomodels, physionet), each with an independent list_fn/entry_fn/id_of; harvest() calls should_process(db, ident, force) before every upsert, keyed by the source's own identifier scheme, so cross-source overwrites are structurally impossible.

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline ModelHarvestStep loads the committed datasets/model_hra_map.json network-free (build_if_missing: false) and emits n_models=1576 (1,096 biomodels + 480 physionet) with a non-empty per_source and coverage summary; scripts/harvest_models.py (the reproducible-refresh CLI) calls the exact same model_harvest.harvest() function, so the Step and the CLI cannot diverge.

biological_validation.basis: The unified BioModels+PhysioNet state is not evaluated for biological correctness here -- BioModels correctness was biomodel-hra-map's job, and this Step reproduces those rows unchanged (F-01). What this study validates is mechanism: the source registry is generic (each source only needs list_fn/entry_fn/id_of) and the identifier-keyed upsert is provably non-destructive across sources (F-02), which is the property that let the PhysioNet harvest add 480 rows without touching any of the 1,096 BioModels rows.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01/F-02 establish, now that the PhysioNet harvest has run against the committed DB, exactly what changed and what didn't: all 1,096 BioModels rows are untouched, 480 PhysioNet rows were added incrementally (124 organ-tagged via the offline keyword table), and the coverage summary mechanism correctly reflects the union of both sources -- giving a precise, falsifiable record of what the harvest run actually did.

limitations: The committed PhysioNet harvest was run with --no-llm, so per_source.physionet=480 reflects only the deterministic keyword table (124 organ-tagged); the LLM-fallback tail was never exercised against the committed DB, so the eventual organ-coverage ceiling once that fallback runs is still unmeasured.

build_if_missing: false means this baseline never exercises the live PhysioNet DataCite enumeration or the keyword/LLM organ-mapping fallback path at all; those are only exercised when the Step (or the CLI) is run with a refresh flag, which is a separate, explicit operation from this study's default baseline.

resolved_uncertainties: A single Step (ModelHarvestStep) can front a multi-source registry (biomodels, physionet) and load the unified DB network-free by default, with the same underlying harvest() function backing the reproducible-refresh CLI -- Step and CLI cannot diverge.
The upsert mechanism is identifier-keyed per source, so it is structurally provable (not just claimed) that a PhysioNet harvest cannot overwrite or drop a BioModels row, and vice versa.
remaining_uncertainties: How many more PhysioNet projects would resolve to an HRA organ if the LLM fallback ran against the 356 projects the keyword table left unmapped (480 - 124 organ-tagged), and how much of the eventual resolution would come from the curated keyword table vs. the LLM fallback? (fp-physionet-llm-fallback.)

Once PhysioNet rows exist, will the corpus-coverage summary (mesh/uniprot/chebi/kegg -- all BioModels-specific annotation types) need a PhysioNet-appropriate analogue, or does it stay meaningfully BioModels-only?

followup_study_proposals.title: Run the PhysioNet LLM organ-mapping fallback and measure the keyword-vs-LLM coverage split
followup_study_proposals.motivation: The committed harvest ran with --no-llm: 480 PhysioNet rows are in the DB and 124 are organ-tagged by the deterministic keyword table alone. The natural next step is to run the LLM fallback (no_llm: false) over the remaining unmapped tail and measure what it adds -- organ coverage, and the keyword-vs-LLM split in physionet_organ_map.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Run model_harvest.harvest(['physionet'], no_llm=False) against datasets/model_hra_map.json, then report per_source.physionet, the resulting organ_to_models coverage for PhysioNet-only rows, and what fraction of organ resolutions came from KEYWORD_TO_ORGAN vs. the LLM fallback.
